metadata.title: Women's Kidney Health in Focus: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
top_takeaways: Women have a higher prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD) than men, yet are less likely to progress to kidney failure, undergo dialysis, or receive a kidney transplant.
Reproductive health factors, including adverse pregnancy outcomes, menopause, and polycystic ovary syndrome, uniquely influence CKD risk and progression in women.
Advancing precision kidney medicine requires equitable healthcare access, integration of reproductive health assessments into chronic care, and adequate representation of women in clinical trials.

recommendations.statement: Family planning, prepregnancy counseling, and antenatal care are essential to support reproductive health in women with chronic kidney disease.
recommendations.target_population: Women with chronic kidney disease of reproductive age
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Family planning, prepregnancy counseling, and antenatal care are essential to support reproductive health in women with chronic kidney disease.

recommendations.statement: Clinical trials in kidney disease must be designed with adequate power and include equitable representation of both women and men to establish sex-specific evidence bases.
recommendations.target_population: Researchers and clinical trial designers studying chronic kidney disease
